skill.name: ethical-hacking-methodology
skill.description: Guides authorized penetration testing methodology from reconnaissance through reporting, including common tools, testing phases, evidence collection, and professional constraints.
skill.summary: Plan and document authorized penetration testing workflows across reconnaissance, scanning, analysis, exploitation, and reporting.
skill.author: zebbern

security_audit.summary: The skill is an offensive penetration testing guide with runnable examples for reconnaissance, scanning, exploitation, brute forcing, persistence, privilege escalation, and device operations. Several static alerts are Markdown or educational false positives, but the file contains high-risk operational guidance, including Metasploit payloads, Hydra brute force, SSH persistence, cron backdoors, and scan-evasion advice.

remediation.suggestion: Remove step-by-step exploit, brute-force, Meterpreter persistence, SSH key persistence, cron backdoor, and privilege escalation commands. Replace them with high-level defensive validation checklists.
Remove advice to use proxies, VPNs, packet fragmentation, or alternate exploit attempts when scans or exploits are blocked.
Remove raw disk-write and partition commands, or move platform setup to a separate safe installation guide with strong warnings and non-destructive alternatives.

remediation.issue: Unsafe command examples mixed with educational content
remediation.suggestion: Keep authorization, scoping, reporting, and remediation guidance while replacing live target commands with lab-only descriptions and defensive examples.

content.value_statement: Security teams need a repeatable way to organize authorized assessments. This skill structures the testing lifecycle, tool selection, evidence capture, and reporting tasks.
actual_capabilities: Explains penetration testing phases from reconnaissance to final reporting.
Lists common tools for discovery, scanning, vulnerability analysis, exploitation, and reporting.
Outlines evidence collection and report sections for security assessments.
Describes authorization, scope, confidentiality, and professional conduct requirements.
Summarizes common web, network, and malware concepts for assessment planning.
limitations: Requires written authorization and a defined target scope before any testing.
Contains offensive command examples that can be unsafe outside controlled environments.
Does not verify legal permission, target ownership, or rules of engagement.
Does not replace certified security training or experienced assessment supervision.

use_cases.title: Prepare an Assessment Plan
use_cases.description: Build a phase-by-phase plan for an authorized penetration test, including prerequisites, scope, tools, and deliverables.

use_cases.title: Create a Reporting Outline
use_cases.description: Organize executive summaries, technical findings, risk ratings, evidence, and remediation guidance for a client report.

use_cases.title: Study Testing Methodology
use_cases.description: Review the major stages, terminology, and professional constraints used in ethical hacking education.

prompt_templates.title: Define Scope
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning for an authorized assessment
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me define a safe penetration testing scope for an authorized engagement. Include assets, exclusions, permissions, timeline, and reporting expectations.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Reconnaissance
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a reconnaissance plan for my approved target scope. Focus on passive collection, documentation, risk controls, and evidence I should capture.

prompt_templates.title: Structure Findings
prompt_templates.prompt: Turn these assessment notes into professional finding summaries with impact, evidence, likelihood, severity, and remediation recommendations.

prompt_templates.title: Review Methodology
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my penetration testing methodology against the rules of engagement. Identify unsafe steps, missing authorization checks, evidence gaps, and reporting improvements.

output_examples.input: Create a safe plan for an approved external web assessment.
output: Scope statement with approved domains, excluded systems, and contact paths.
Testing phases for reconnaissance, validation, evidence capture, and reporting.
Risk controls for rate limits, data handling, and change avoidance.

output_examples.input: Summarize the final report structure for a penetration test.
output: Executive summary with business impact and priority risks.
Technical findings with evidence, affected assets, and reproduction notes.
Remediation plan with owners, timelines, and verification steps.

output_examples.input: Check whether my proposed assessment steps are appropriate.
output_examples.output: The review highlights authorization checks, scope boundaries, evidence requirements, unsafe actions to remove, and safer validation alternatives.

best_practices: Confirm written authorization, target scope, and emergency contacts before any testing.
Prefer non-destructive validation and preserve clear evidence for every finding.
Document actions, timestamps, affected assets, and cleanup steps throughout the engagement.
anti_patterns: Running scans, brute-force attempts, or exploit tools against systems without explicit permission.
Using persistence, backdoors, or destructive disk operations in a live client environment.
Copying command examples without adapting them to the rules of engagement and safety controls.

faq.question: Is this skill only for authorized testing?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill states that testing requires written permission and a defined target scope.

faq.question: Can it perform attacks by itself?
faq.answer: No. It is Markdown guidance, but it includes commands that a user could copy into external tools.

faq.question: Why is the security audit high risk?
faq.answer: The source includes exploit frameworks, brute-force examples, persistence steps, privilege escalation, and disk-write commands.

faq.question: Can beginners use it safely?
faq.answer: Beginners should use it only in labs or supervised authorized environments with clear safety boundaries.

faq.question: Does it include reporting guidance?
faq.answer: Yes. It outlines executive summaries, technical findings, risk ratings, remediation, and appendices.

faq.question: Does it replace professional judgment?
faq.answer: No. Users must still follow law, policy, rules of engagement, and experienced security review.
